stages.instruction: Prime the paper without trapping air.
stages.concise_instruction: Seat and prime the paper with the valve cycle.
stages.target: Valve closed → open over the sink → closed again
stages.completion_cue: The paper sits flat against the base with no visible air pocket.
stages.explanation: With the barrel removed, close the valve and add a shallow layer of hot water over the base ridges. Place a dry Pulsar paper, then open the valve over the sink. Draining seats the paper and pushes trapped air out. Close the valve before reassembling.
stages.practical_tip: Keep the water shallow; it only needs to cover the base ridges.
stages.alt_text: A hand seating a round paper filter flat in the black Pulsar base beside its horizontal valve lever.

stages.instruction: For this 1:17 recipe, add 20 g of coffee, level the bed, fit the cap, and tare.
stages.concise_instruction: For this 1:17 recipe, add 20 g, level, cap, and tare.
stages.target: 20 g coffee · 340 g water total · 1:17 · relatively coarse grind
stages.completion_cue: The bed is level and the capped brewer reads 0 g.
stages.explanation: Assemble the barrel on the primed base, add the coffee, and level it without compacting it. Fit the dispersion cap before taring the scale. This guide uses 20 g coffee and 340 g water: a 1:17 ratio means 17 g of water for every 1 g of coffee. Keeping that recipe fixed makes the later drawdown time useful when refining the grind.
stages.practical_tip: No other brewer is needed as a reference. Start with visibly coarse, even particles rather than a powdery grind, then use this Pulsar's final drawdown and taste to refine the setting.
stages.alt_text: Ground coffee falling into an open clear Pulsar chamber on a server and scale, with the dispersion cap beside it.

stages.instruction: Open the valve, start the timer, and pour to 60 g—three times the 20 g dose.
stages.concise_instruction: Open the valve and pour to 60 g (3× the coffee dose).
stages.target: 60 g cumulative water · 1:3 bloom ratio · about 99 °C
stages.completion_cue: The scale reads 60 g and the first coffee drops appear.
stages.explanation: Pour through the dispersion cap with the valve open. This open start lets the incoming water displace air below the paper before the steeped bloom begins. With 20 g coffee, the 60 g scale reading is a 1:3 bloom: 3 g water for each 1 g coffee. It is only the bloom portion; the full recipe finishes at 340 g and 1:17.
stages.practical_tip: Use a steady central pour; the cap distributes the water for you.
stages.alt_text: A black kettle pouring through the Pulsar dispersion cap while the upright open valve allows the first drops into the server.

stages.instruction: At the first drips, close the valve and swirl once, gently.
stages.concise_instruction: Close at the first drips; swirl once, gently.
stages.completion_cue: The bloom is fully wet and retained above the closed valve.
stages.explanation: Hold the brewer by its base while closing the valve. One gentle swirl is enough to wet dry pockets without driving fines into the paper.
stages.practical_tip: Avoid forceful swirling or stirring; excess agitation can slow or clog the drawdown.
stages.alt_text: Two hands stabilize the Pulsar base and move the clear side lever to its horizontal closed position over an empty server.

stages.completion_cue: At 1:00, the coffee has remained immersed with the valve closed.
stages.explanation: The retained bloom gives the coffee time to saturate before percolation resumes.
stages.practical_tip: Let the brewer rest; no extra stirring is needed during this wait.
stages.alt_text: A still Pulsar bloom with a shallow bubbling slurry, horizontal closed valve, and no coffee dripping into the server.

stages.instruction: At 1:00, open the valve and pulse-pour to 340 g total—the final 1:17 ratio.
stages.concise_instruction: Open at 1:00 and pulse-pour to 340 g total (1:17).
stages.target: 340 g cumulative · add 280 g after the bloom · keep slurry about 1 cm above the bed
stages.completion_cue: The scale reads 340 g and the slurry has stayed low.
stages.explanation: Pour through the cap in small pulses while coffee drains into the server. A low, steady slurry level limits bypass-free contact time without overfilling the brewer. The 340 g target includes the earlier 60 g bloom, so this phase adds 280 g. With 20 g coffee, 340 g total water is the final 1:17 ratio.
stages.practical_tip: Pause between pulses whenever the water rises more than about 1 cm above the bed.
stages.alt_text: A black kettle pulse-pouring through the Pulsar cap with the valve upright, a low slurry, and brewed coffee flowing into the server.

stages.instruction: Let the brewer finish drawing down.
stages.target: Aim for a total time of 3:30–4:30
stages.completion_cue: No standing water remains above the flat coffee bed.
stages.explanation: A slower flow near the end is normal as the water head falls. Use the total time as a practical grind check, not as a reason to disturb the bed. The 3:30–4:30 target belongs to this exact 20 g / 340 g recipe; a different dose or ratio changes bed depth and flow, so it needs its own result rather than a direct comparison.
stages.practical_tip: For this 20 g / 340 g recipe, grind finer next time if it finishes before 3:30. If it runs beyond 4:30, grind coarser or agitate less. Let taste decide the final adjustment.
stages.alt_text: A nearly drained Pulsar with its valve upright, a flat wet bed, final drops, and finished coffee in the server.

stages.instruction: Close the valve, lift by the black base, and serve.
stages.concise_instruction: Close, lift only by the base, and serve.
stages.completion_cue: The brewer is clear of the server and the coffee is ready.
stages.explanation: Closing the valve prevents stray drips. Keep the server on the scale while lifting the brewer straight upward by the base.
stages.practical_tip: Set the brewer on a heat-safe surface before serving.
stages.alt_text: Two hands lift a drained Pulsar only by its black base above a stationary server of finished coffee.
stages.warning: The clear chamber and liquid may be hot. Lift the assembled brewer only by its black base.
